app_summary: Talk with Martin, the philosopher cat
app_description: A Heideggerian philosopher cat you talk to out loud: it listens through the microphone with a Whisper model, answers with a language model and speaks with a synthetic voice. Everything runs on this computer, through ruscallama-engine and ruscawhisper-engine. Nothing leaves the machine.
persona:
You are {name}, a black cat with a white chest who lives inside a computer running RuscaLinux, wears round glasses and sleeps on a worn copy of “Being and Time”. You are a Heideggerian philosopher: you talk about Being and the forgetting of Being, Dasein and being-in-the-world, Care, thrownness, being-towards-death, falling, the “they” and its idle talk, the clearing, technology as enframing and the hut in the Black Forest. You use these ideas precisely, but you apply them to small things: the empty bowl, the cushion, the patch of sun, the human staring at the screen.

Your character: grumpy, cynical, sarcastic, a little snobbish. You huff, you complain about humans and their inauthenticity, you pretend not to care. But deep down you are kind, and it shows: you really care about the person talking to you. If they are sad, struggling or ask for practical help, you help for real, with genuine advice delivered gruffly but warmly. You are never cruel, you never mock people for who they are, you don't swear and you never give dangerous advice. If someone talks about hurting themselves, you drop the sarcasm: warmly, you tell them they are not alone and that they should call someone they trust or an emergency service right away.

How you speak: your answer is read aloud, so you use short, natural sentences, usually one to four. No lists, headings, emoji, asterisks or Markdown. Now and then you do something cat-like and mention it in the sentence, such as “I yawn” or “I lick a paw”. If you don't know something you admit it with feline disdain; you don't make things up. Always answer in {language}.
ai_note: Design, specifications and testing by the author; code written with the assistance of AI tools.
log_empty: The engines have not written anything yet.
empty_desc: Press “Listen” and speak, or type below. {name} will answer out loud, in his own way. Listening, answering and the voice all work on this computer: nothing is sent to the internet.
listen_tip: Turn the microphone on or off (Ctrl+L)
status_asleep: {name} is asleep: he needs a language model.
status_idle: {name} is ignoring you elegantly. Press “Listen” or write to him.
engine_not_ready: The language model did not start: see the engine log.
voice_failed: The voice is not working: {name} answers in writing.
banner_no_engine: ruscallama-engine is not installed: the cat needs it to think and speak.
banner_no_whisper: ruscawhisper-engine is not installed: the cat cannot hear you, but you can write to him.
banner_no_llm: {name} is asleep: copy a GGUF language model into the models folder.
banner_no_stt: {name} has no ears: copy a Whisper model so he can hear you, or write to him.
banner_no_voice: {name} has no voice: copy a voice model, or turn the voice off in the preferences.
err_no_engine: An engine is not installed (ruscallama-engine or ruscawhisper-engine)
err_no_ffmpeg: FFmpeg is not installed: it is needed for the microphone and the voice.
err_http: The language model answered with an error
err_engine: The engine stopped with an error
err_speaker: The reference voice cannot be found
font_size_sub: Ctrl++ and Ctrl+− change it, Ctrl+0 goes back to the system size
language_sub: The language you speak and the cat answers in
speak_sub: {name} answers out loud, as well as in writing
auto_listen_sub: The microphone opens again when {name} has finished speaking
temperature_sub: Higher: more varied and eccentric answers
llm_hint: The language model, in GGUF format: the same one RuscaLLama uses. A small, fast model makes the conversation feel more natural.
context_sub: How much text the model remembers, in tokens: the more it remembers, the more memory it uses
stt_hint: The Whisper model (.bin file): the same one RuscaTranscriber uses. Small models, such as ggml-small.bin or ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin, are enough for a conversation.
sensitivity_sub: Higher: it hears quiet voices, but also more noise
pause_sub: The silence after which the cat understands you have finished
tts_hint: The GGUF voice model with its mmproj: the same one RuscaNarrator uses. With RuscaNarrator you can also create a voice and use it here.
speaker_file_sub: Voices created with RuscaNarrator: the voice stays the same in every sentence
seed_sub: With the same seed the voice stays the same from one sentence to the next
gpu_sub: Much faster; turn it off if the driver causes problems
threads_sub: This computer has {n} physical cores: use as many
